entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (method). A pulse of heavy amino acids separates newly made from pre-existing protein by mass, so synthesis and degradation can be read without cycloheximide; half-lives from about 10 to over 1,000 hours are reported for thousands of proteins in non-dividing cells including mouse embryonic neurons.
entries.snippet: Peptides of pre-existing and newly synthesized proteins were distinguished by their mass due to incorporation of light or heavy arginine and lysine.

experimental_context.system: Dynamic SILAC mass spectrometry of protein turnover in five non-dividing primary cell types (human B cells, NK cells, monocytes, hepatocytes; mouse embryonic cortical neurons); proteome-wide half-lives; NOT a WWOX system and no variant protein
experimental_context.endpoint: protein half-lives, reproducibility between replicates, complex-level coherence

entries.proposition: Labelling windows range from 6 to 72 hours, so proteins with half-lives shorter than a few hours (as many destabilised variants have) fall outside the measured range; the abstract states a range from 10 hours and the fast example given is a kinase at about 9 to 11 hours in B cells.
entries.snippet: Janus kinase 3, which is predominantly expressed in the cells of hematopoietic lineage has a very short half-life between 9 and 11 h

entries.proposition: Coverage is 4,667 to 6,534 protein groups per cell type and a quality filter (regression R-squared above 0.85) kept 8,804 half-lives; a protein not detected cannot be given a half-life.
entries.snippet: This criterion was fulfilled by 8804 proteins taken together across the five cell types.

entries.proposition: Replicate agreement is high (R-squared of log half-lives 0.91 to 0.94; 98 percent of half-lives within two-fold), but cell types differ: hepatocytes and mouse neurons differ substantially from the haematopoietic cells.
entries.snippet: For 98% of all protein half-lives from the high-quality data set, the replicates differed by less than two-fold.

entries.proposition: Complex subunits tend to turn over together, so the half-life of a protein is partly set by the assembly it belongs to; for a missense variant of a subunit this predicts different turnover in assembled and free states.
entries.snippet: A clear and significant trend (p-value < 0.001, Wilcoxon-rank test) for a more coherent half-life distribution of protein subunits within individual complexes becomes apparent for all cell types
